label: dam-probes-p27-p28-p26b
_why: ENGINE PROBES (user, 2026-09-28 18:18: "Run both, you have until 20:00 to START any probe that's anticipated to take no more than 20 minutes"). Two questions left open by FINDINGS F176. (1) p27 / p28: a survey's bureaucracy cost reaches bureaucracy_usage only at the next recalculation, so the spare check in `possible` overshoots when one AI pass takes several surveys (p24). p27 adds a 30-day 'just took a survey' country variable, set in when_taken and required absent in `possible`; p28 is the same book WITHOUT it (the control). Both give the ten majors a flat +4,000 bureaucracy (dams.probe.bureaucracy_bonus) so they hold room for several surveys at once from 1836. Otherwise = config/mod_config.probe-dam-p19.json (the AI takes the survey decision; spare >= cost in possible; 2-month surveys; construction x0.05). (2) p26b: p26 (open builders; the ten majors hold every survey) with the host's withdrawal from its investment-rights treaties 90 days, not a year, into a foreign construction in an independent non-major's state, so the build is caught mid-progress.

_questions.Q1 (p27 vs p28): Does the cooldown stop same-day multiple takes and the bureaucracy overshoot, while still letting a major run several surveys at once (one new take a month)?
_questions.Q2 (p26b): When the host withdraws from its investment-rights treaties while a foreign government's dam construction in its state is progressing, is the construction cancelled (progress lost, per the wiki's queue rule), kept, or completed?

_predictions.Q1: p28: same-day multiples and deficits of 1-3 surveys' cost; p27: none, 2-4 surveys running at once per major within a year
_predictions.Q2: cancelled, as a released subject's construction is (F176 section 2); a null is possible if no foreign build lands in a non-major independent state by 1851

_cost: 2 runs x 1836 -> 1846.1 (~12 min each) + 1 run x 1836 -> 1851.1 (~17 min), about 45 minutes
_caveats: Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30).
Probe builds: technologies and bureaucracy granted, costs shrunk - no economic reading.
